title: Approval decision surfaces
description: Objective: implement exact-hash plan, expansion, delta-reapproval, acceptance, confirmation, and cutover decision surfaces. Deliverable: approval modules with reason-coded disabled states. NOT in scope: mutable policy editing or implicit approval. Hard dependencies: Generated control-room client and Policy approval core. Owned paths: apps/control-room/src/approvals/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test.
definitionOfDone: Every decision shows exact subject hash, scope, risk, budget, policy, delta, and consequences.
Disabled actions expose stable reason codes and no stale approval can submit.
Manual default and audited default-off automation are represented accurately.
taskRails: The standalone control room displays daemon truth and nextAllowedCommands; it never derives authority, readiness, or evidence strength.
Every fact is text/icon/color encoded, keyboard accessible, provenance-drillable, and honest under degraded data.
IDE adapters remain thin optional launch/discover/embed shells with no product logic. Keep modules below 400 lines; explicit owned paths only.

Tests assert exact codes + which guard refused; mutation red-checks named (disable the validity guard -> stale test red; disable the hash match -> mismatch test red). Confirm RED.

REASON CHANNEL IS SELF-CHECKING (stronger than the plan's fixed code list, which step-1 showed was partly wrong): approvalReason(code, source, phrase) calls lookupRuntimeError(code) and throws if (a) the descriptor's code !== the requested code — which is exactly how an invented spelling is caught, since unknown spellings fall back to UNKNOWN_ERROR — or (b) the row's validSources is non-empty and does not list the claimed source. Empty validSources is source-unrestricted by contract (CAPABILITY_DENIED). All seven APPROVAL_REASONS entries are therefore registry-checked at module load. Tests assert the throw for a forbidden pair (CUTOVER_STATE_INVALID + GOAL) and for an invented code, and assert the exact §8.1 sentence "Unavailable: {phrase} (CODE)."

FIXTURE INTEGRITY REFUSALS (design 701/710): approvalRecord/withRecord refuse a SYSTEM_POLICY record claiming HUMAN_APPROVED truth, and refuse one carrying R2/R3. Tests assert both throws by message.

approval-gating.ts (PURE, no JSX): controlTestId (spec §1.4 dot->dash + qualifier), unavailableText, decisionCommandKind (EXPANSION -> graph.approve, all others -> approval.decide; provisional per §13-D1), resolveApprovalControls, isSubmittable. Guard chain, order fixed and PINNED BY TEST: (1) no matching affordance -> supplied reason ? DISABLED : ABSENT, refusedBy AFFORDANCE_ABSENT; (2) lifecycle !== PENDING -> ILLEGAL_TRANSITION/RECORD_LIFECYCLE; (3) validity INVALIDATED -> REVISION_REBOUND, SUPERSEDED -> SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY, both RECORD_VALIDITY; (4) affordance pins no graphRevisionHash -> STALE_EPOCH/REVISION_HASH (fail-closed), or pinned hash !== record.exactRevisionHash -> EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT/REVISION_HASH; (5) ENABLED. DoD-2 structural belt: every refusing path returns commandId null, so a surface cannot submit a stale approval even if it ignores `state`.

Tests assert the specific reason code AND which guard refused on every failure path (never merely "did not succeed"), pin guard precedence with a record that violates two guards at once, and sweep all 9 kinds x 2 stale validities asserting swept === 9*2 and > 0 so a silently-empty sweep cannot pass. Fixture affordances are validated through the daemon's real buildNextAllowedCommands parser rather than only asserted.

DEVIATION FROM PLAN TEXT (documented, not silent): the plan's asserted list of codes "whose validSources include APPROVAL/CUTOVER" is inaccurate for STALE_EPOCH / EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT / SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY / REVISION_REBOUND (their rows list GRAPH_REVISION, not APPROVAL). Since an approval is pinned to a graph revision, each reason declares GRAPH_REVISION as its source and the registry check enforces it — no invented codes, and the pairing is machine-verified instead of asserted by hand.

Mutation red-checks for these guards are deliberately deferred to step-5, where the plan collects the full battery.
